brief.headline: Close the ₹1.26 Cr gap to Sayaji's price and secure ₹1.74 Cr cash by paying on delivery instead of 30 days later.

priceAsk.summary: Match the ₹66.48/KG we pay Sayaji Industries for identical Dextrose.
priceAsk.basis: We already buy the same material from Sayaji at ₹66.48/KG — our price with Gujarat Ambuja is ₹68.45/KG, a 3.0% gap. The open market shows Dextrose typically trades ₹66–73/kg, so ₹66.48/KG sits right in that fair band.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Move to payment on delivery (cash-on-receipt) from the current 30 days after receipt.
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Frees up ₹1.74 Cr of cash for us that's currently tied up waiting 30 days.

brief.financialLeverage: Gujarat Ambuja is a large, healthy supplier (₹5995.63 Cr revenue) and keeps 8.5% of every rupee they sell — comfortable room to move on price. But we're tiny to them: our ₹21.21 Cr is just 0.35% of their sales, so we have limited pull from size alone. The real leverage is dual-sourcing: they supply 56% of our Dextrose, making us dependent, but Sayaji already proves we can get the exact item cheaper, and Gulshan Polyols (₹2359.06 Cr, health score B 62/100) and Sanstar (₹821.13 Cr, health C 57/100) are ready alternates — we can credibly walk if they won't match the market.

evidence.point: We pay Gujarat Ambuja 3.0% more than Sayaji for the same Dextrose
evidence.figure: Gap: 3.0%, costing us ₹1.26 Cr per year

evidence.point: Their profit margin is a comfortable 8.5%, so a price cut won't hurt them
We're a very small customer to them — only 0.35% of their business
evidence.figure: Our spend as share of their revenue: 0.35%

evidence.point: The open market shows our current price is fair but on the higher side of typical
evidence.figure: Market typical band: ₹66–73/kg; verdict: MARKET-FAIR (slightly favourable)

evidence.point: Switching to cash-on-delivery frees up ₹1.74 Cr of our cash
They dominate our Dextrose supply at 56%, creating single-source risk
evidence.figure: Spend with them: ₹21.21 Cr (56% of material)

alternates.name: Gulshan Polyols Ltd
alternates.why: Listed starch maker (₹2359.06 Cr revenue, health B 62/100) — an established dextrose supplier and a drop-in alternate; stronger financially than Gujarat Ambuja's C rating.

alternates.name: Sanstar Ltd
alternates.why: Recently-listed maize-derivatives specialist (₹821.13 Cr, health C 57/100) focused on starch and dextrose — growing capacity, credible second source.

alternates.name: Tirupati Starch & Chemicals Ltd
alternates.why: Listed Indore wet-miller (₹365.39 Cr) making Dextrose ANHYDROUS in IV-fluid grade — exact product match; confirm IP monograph certificate before switching (health D 27/100, so audit carefully).

risks: Gujarat Ambuja supplies 56% of our Dextrose (₹21.21 Cr) — pushing too hard without a qualified second source in place puts continuity at risk.
We're only 0.35% of their revenue, so they can easily walk away if we squeeze; line up Gulshan or Sanstar with an RFQ before the meeting.
Tirupati's health score is weak (D 27/100) — if we trial them, keep Gujarat Ambuja live until Tirupati proves stable supply.
The market ask verdict is 'MARKET-FAIR (slightly favourable)' — our ₹68.45/KG isn't wildly out of line, so frame the ask around matching Sayaji (₹66.48/KG), not a general 'you're overcharging' claim.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to align your Dextrose price to the ₹66.48/KG we already pay Sayaji for identical material, and move to payment on delivery to free up working cash — let's find a path that works for both sides.
